compatibility.statement: `/` applied to two `Int` operands is a compile error. A program written against the original decision, which expected `7 / 2` to yield a fractional value, no longer compiles.
compatibility.result: 4 sites, and all four are the `reject_slash_operator.kofun` fixtures that exist to be refused: one each for the native, self-host C11, wasm32, and numeric-conformance paths. No other tracked Kofun source applies `/` to `Int` operands.

implementation.enablement: Enabled unconditionally, with no flag. The frontend refuses `/` on `Int` before lowering, and the native x86-64, native AArch64, wasm32 and self-host C11 paths each carry their own refusal fixture so no backend can quietly give the operator a meaning.

amendments.delta: `/` is no longer an `Int` operator at all. It is reserved and refused with one diagnostic rather than returning a fractional value, because no fractional type exists to return. `//` is unchanged and remains floor division.
amendments.original_semantics: `/` returns floating division. `//` performs integer/floor division.

compatibility.statement: Three documents said `/` on `Int` yielded `Float` while four backends truncated and one refused the operator outright. The amendment makes refusal the single stated meaning, so the documents and the backends agree.
compatibility.result: 12 numeric conformance cases execute on every declared backend. The only case applying `/` is `reject_slash_operator.kofun`, and every declared backend refuses it identically.

rfcs.title: No silent backend fallback

compatibility.statement: No accepted program changes meaning. The decision constrains implementations: a backend that cannot lower a construct must fail with a source-located error or be recorded as unsupported, and may not substitute a different construct.

implementation.enablement: Enabled for every registered backend/corpus pair. `tests/conformance/capabilities.tsv` is the closed manifest of supported and unsupported pairs; adapters no longer carry an independently authoritative corpus list, so a backend cannot declare its own coverage.

rfcs.title: Typed hygienic macros

compatibility.statement: Nothing is implemented, so no program changes meaning. The decision binds a future implementation: quote and unquote operate on token trees or a typed public AST, and there is no C-style textual preprocessor.

rfcs.title: Algebraic laws are compiler artifacts

compatibility.statement: Nothing is implemented, so no accepted program changes meaning. The decision binds a future implementation: `law` is contextual, family names are ordinary identifiers, and a family, implementation, and check request remain separate source declarations.

rfcs.title: Evidence levels are never conflated

compatibility.statement: Nothing emits executable law evidence, so no accepted program or artifact changes meaning. The decision constrains future checkers to compute and preserve distinct `bounded-exhaustive`, `proven-finite`, and `proven` assurance levels under deterministic finite evaluation.

rfcs.title: Versioned machine-readable law evidence

compatibility.statement: `kofun.law-evidence/v2` is deliberately incompatible with v1. A v1 document is historical migration material and is never interpreted as v2, so no v1 evidence can authorize a v2 optimization or cache hit. Nothing emits either version yet, so nothing in the repository is affected today.

rfcs.title: Records declare with `type` and construct with labels

compatibility.statement: The bounded record frontend adds nominal declarations and labelled construction without changing the meaning of an existing accepted program. The main compiler and backends do not enable this surface yet.

implementation.enablement: Enabled only in the bounded record frontend invoked by `task records`. Module visibility, generic records, the main compiler, and backend lowering remain outside the checkpoint.

rfcs.title: Four semantic namespaces

compatibility.statement: Assigning every declaration to one of four syntax-directed namespaces adds an identity domain rather than a restriction. Capitalization stays non-semantic, no source form that resolves today is refused by this decision, and the namespace tag becomes a new input to identity and serialization.

rfcs.title: An explicit `module` header is the only module authority

compatibility.statement: Breaking for two shapes: a manifest source with no `module` header, and an anonymous single-file operand that carries one. Both are refused rather than given a fallback identity, because a fallback would make a file move a semantic rename.
compatibility.corpus_query: git grep -lE '^module ' -- '*.kofun' | wc -l; git ls-files '*.kofun' | wc -l
compatibility.result: 96 of 677 tracked Kofun sources declare a header. All 96 sit under `tests/conformance/` module, ADT-exhaustiveness, and incremental fixtures; no tracked example, benchmark, stdlib, or bootstrap source carries one.

rfcs.title: One digest never does two jobs

compatibility.statement: KIF, the framed SHA-256 preimage, and the three separate semantic and ABI digests are a new compiler-authoritative interface format. No source program changes meaning, and no existing artifact is reinterpreted: a v1 identity exists only where the versioned envelope was written.

rfcs.title: Re-exports are explicit and never widen

compatibility.statement: `pub` on an import is new surface. An ordinary `import` keeps its meaning as a private binding, and no declaration becomes publicly reachable without the modifier.
compatibility.result: 8 tracked sources use the form: 5 re-export fixtures, 1 import-alias fixture, and 2 incremental fixtures. Every one of them was written for this decision's gates.

implementation.enablement: Same-package `pub import` and `pub from` in the Stage 2 frontend, with non-widening `ExportBindingId` edges and the stated bounds: 64-edge chains, 1,024 bindings per module, 65,536 edges per package. There is no `internal` re-export form, and cross-package re-export is outside the checkpoint.

rfcs.title: The typed sidecar is never authoritative

compatibility.statement: The sidecar is a new artifact that no compiler path reads. It is emitted on request, declares `"authoritative": false`, and cannot become an input, so no program or build changes meaning.

implementation.enablement: Stage 2 projects compiler-derived semantic events one-way into typed-sidecar v1 for an explicit single-file `kofun check`. The document is non-authoritative, and compiler, KIF, and cache consumers are refused by the authority-boundary gate.

rfcs.title: Discovery is compiler-backed

compatibility.statement: The `kofun.discovery.request/v1` and `kofun.discovery.result/v1` records are a new tooling surface. Results are non-authoritative and forbidden as compiler, KIF, build, or release input, so nothing that compiles today changes meaning.

rfcs.title: Unsuffixed fractional literals are `Decimal`

compatibility.statement: Breaking for a program that relies on an unsuffixed fractional literal denoting `Float`: under this decision it denotes `Decimal`, and a binary64 value requires the explicit suffix. Mixed `Int`, `Decimal`, and `Float` arithmetic is refused rather than promoted.
compatibility.result: 20 sites in 11 tracked sources. 8 are fixtures that exist to assert this rule -- `d001`, `e2s99`, `e2s100`, `e2s101`, `e2s103`, the two `reject_` numeric conformance fixtures, and the Stage 2 decimal token fixture. The other 12 sites, in `tests/kofun/scientific.kofun`, `examples/science.kofun` and `benchmarks/vector.kofun`, pass unsuffixed literals into Float-shaped scientific calls and need the suffix.

rfcs.title: Type-level programming is named and terminating

compatibility.statement: The `kofun.type-reduction/default-v1` profile adds a module-level declaration form. Anonymous type expressions and general recursive type programs are refused by the profile rather than removed from the language, because neither form exists today.
compatibility.result: 0 sites. No tracked Kofun source declares a type-level function.

rfcs.title: `trait`, with a local-trait-or-local-outer-type orphan rule

compatibility.statement: The orphan rule and the dictionary-passing baseline constrain implementations written after them; the specification marks the lowering baseline as provisional until its experiment is recorded, and the coherence rule as accepted. The bounded frontend that enforces the rule is gated by `task traits`, and the state stays `accepted` because release/claims.json records no capability claim for it.
compatibility.result: 18 files, all under `tests/conformance/traits` and written for the bounded #332 frontend, which refuses a foreign trait implemented for a foreign type with `E2S131`. No other tracked source declares a trait or an implementation.

rfcs.title: Layout is target-parameterized, not target-identical

compatibility.statement: The contract defines byte layout only and does not change code generation. A backend that does not claim AggregateLayout v1 is unaffected; one that does must agree with the golden vectors, and its own check asserts that a 32-bit and a 64-bit target do not produce identical descriptors.

rfcs.title: Validation accumulates in `Validated`, not `Result`

compatibility.statement: `Validated`, its combinators, and the opaque `Issues[E]` are new surface beside `Result`, which keeps its meaning. The five questions the design left open were decided as recommended; a later change to the states, operations, ordering, effect rule, ownership boundary, or complexity bound is an amendment to this decision.
compatibility.result: 0 files. No tracked Kofun source mentions `Validated`, and no library, compiler path, or backend implements the contract.

rfcs.title: Laws are library declarations checked by a finite-model engine

compatibility.statement: `law`, `instance`, and `model` are new contextual top-level declarations; no family name is a keyword. The active compiler rejects every existing `law` example today, so no program changes meaning when the declarations start to parse.
compatibility.result: 3 files, all historical examples that `kofun check` currently rejects with E2S02; none participates in a build.

rfcs.title: Result propagation is postfix `?`, monomorphic to `Result`

compatibility.statement: Postfix `?` on expressions is currently a parse error, so giving it Result-propagation meaning breaks no existing program. `T?` in type position keeps its DD-002 meaning untouched.
compatibility.result: 17 sites, and every one is a `T?` optional type suffix in type position; no tracked source contains an expression-position postfix `?`.

rfcs.title: Streams are a library protocol with explicit demand

compatibility.statement: `Stream[T, E]`, `Subscription`, and the demand/overflow contract are new library surface; no language keyword is added and `Channel` remains a distinct abstraction behind an explicit adapter.
compatibility.result: 0 files. No tracked Kofun source mentions `Stream`, and no library, compiler path, or backend implements the protocol.

rfcs.title: The standard library ships in four tiers

compatibility.statement: The charter assigns tiers, states, and update policy to library capabilities; it changes no program semantics. The machine-checked matrix keeps every coverage claim bounded by evidence.

rfcs.title: The HTTP client is bounded, capability-explicit, HTTP/1.1 first

compatibility.statement: The client is a new T3 module; the closed #24 HTTP server framework keeps its documented bounded profile and is not evidence for this contract. No client is implemented.
compatibility.result: 0 files. No tracked Kofun source calls the proposed client API.

rfcs.title: Time is six types; zones are versioned data; clocks are capabilities

compatibility.statement: Civil types, `Resolve` disambiguation, RFC 3339 profiles, and versioned tz data are new surface. The stdlib/clock seed keeps its syscall-level per-clock `Instant`; the portable contract absorbs that boundary rather than changing it.
compatibility.result: 2 files, both in the stdlib/clock syscall seed; no civil calendar, zone, or RFC 3339 code exists.

rfcs.title: Benchmarks are declared, raw-sample-first, and honest about counters

compatibility.statement: `bench` declarations, the `Bench` API, and the kofun.bench-report/v1 schema are new surface; repository benchmark scripts remain internal evidence and no public harness exists.
compatibility.result: 0 files. No tracked Kofun source declares a benchmark.

rfcs.title: Allocator choice is a scoped, effect-tracked capability

compatibility.statement: Everything proposed is new surface: the `alloc` effect label, the `Alloc` capability and its authority derivation, region-tagged values, diagnostics E340-E343 and R030, capability-taking standard-library variants, and a contextual `with` allocator scope. The managed default stays the default and existing signatures keep their meaning, so no tracked program changes meaning or stops compiling.

rfcs.title: Environment access requires attenuated affine authority

compatibility.statement: Everything proposed is new target surface: runtime-created `RootAuthority`, key-bounded affine `EnvironmentAuthority`, portable `EnvironmentKey`, explicit derivation and attenuation, diagnostics E350-E356, and audit-only package metadata. No existing safe environment API changes, RFC-0001 is unchanged, and no tracked Kofun source collides with these names.

rfcs.title: Scoped parallelism uses lexical spawn/join ownership

compatibility.statement: The lexical `par` scope, direct scope-token `spawn`, consuming `join`, second-class task handles, ownership conflict classes, and bounded model are new target semantics. No released parser accepts the forms, no existing accepted program changes meaning, and no tracked Kofun source uses the proposed surface.
compatibility.result: 0 matches across 799 tracked `.kofun` sources at 516e8fb3925088dd64b291e8cd749764a41891b1; grep exits 1 with no output, so no tracked source uses the proposed `par`, `.spawn(`, or `.join(` surface.

rfcs.title: Ownership kind is classified structurally through ADTs, tuples, and generic instantiation

compatibility.statement: The proposal adds refusals to types that already exist, so it is not purely additive. The breaking shape is stated exactly: a program that places an owned value inside a record, tuple, ADT constructor payload, closure capture, `Optional`, `List`, or generic instantiation, and then uses that composite where a managed kind is required (`E360`-`E364`). The two-point Managed/Owned lattice, the structural join, the K-SUBST/K-PARAM generic rules, the `List[T]` owned-element refusal, and the four kind constraints are otherwise new surface. The owned domain does not parse in any compiler slice today, so no tracked program can express the refused shape yet.
compatibility.corpus_query: git grep -lE '^[[:space:]]*let[[:space:]]+own[[:space:]]' -- '*.kofun' | wc -l; git grep -nE '\b(trait|impl)[[:space:]]+(Copy|Managed|Owned)\b|:[[:space:]]*(Copy|Managed|Owned)\b' -- '*.kofun' | wc -l; git ls-files -- '*.kofun' | wc -l

Five of 824 tracked `.kofun` sources bind an owned value, and all five were read: examples/ownership.kofun, stdlib/tests/file_roundtrip.kofun, tests/conformance/syntax/issues_35_47/structural_surface.kofun, tests/conformance/syntax/issues_35_47/unsupported_owned_binding.kofun, and tests/kofun/ownership.kofun. None places its owned binding in a record, tuple, ADT payload, list, closure capture, or generic instantiation, so the count of tracked programs carrying the refused shape is 0. The second query returns 0: no tracked source declares or bounds on `Copy`, `Managed`, or `Owned`; `Copy` occurs in tracked `.kofun` sources only inside comments and one E007 message string.

rfcs.title: A trait or type member scope is closed under direct declaration

compatibility.statement: Every shape the rule refuses is already refused, so only the message changes: `E370` replaces a parameter-scope refusal, `E371` replaces a delimiter parse error, and `E372` replaces a slice-boundary message. New surface is the member key (owner identity, namespace, normalized name), the closure rule, the statement that a field collides with an associated value under one type owner but never with a trait method, and the three codes. No accepted program changes meaning and none stops compiling: a member scope with no inherited and no default member has no collision an accepted program could already contain.
compatibility.corpus_query: git ls-files -- '*.kofun' | wc -l; git grep -nwE 'extends|override' -- '*.kofun' | wc -l; git grep -nE '^(trait|foreign trait|impl)|^    fn ' -- '*.kofun' | awk -F: '{ sub(/^[^:]*:[^:]*:/, "") } $0 ~ /^(trait|foreign trait|impl)/ { if (n > 1) m++; n = 0; b++; next } { n++ } END { if (n > 1) m++; print b, m + 0 }'

Of 888 tracked `.kofun` sources, 0 name an inheritance edge or an override marker, and of the 42 trait and implementation member scopes they declare, 0 declare more than one member. So the count of tracked programs this rule refuses that are accepted today is 0, and the count that would need an override marker is 0. The same query returns `890`, `1`, and `45 1` after this change, and both differences are the two negative fixtures it adds: tests/conformance/traits/inherited_member_source.kofun is the one source spelling `extends`, and tests/conformance/traits/member_name_collision.kofun is the one owner declaring two members. Both are refused by the frontend today and pinned by byte-exact goldens, so the count of *accepted* programs in either shape stays 0.

rfcs.title: A module-level binding is language surface, and v1 is the immutable integer constant

compatibility.statement: Every shape v1 admits is refused today by `E2S02`, so no program that compiles changes meaning and none stops compiling. New surface is the module constant declaration `let NAME = <integer literal>`, the rule that it is not a lexical binding and is therefore shadowed rather than redefined by a function-local `let` of the same name, its lowering to one file-scope `static const int64_t`, and the three codes E2S159, E2S160 and E2S161. Those three sit in a free range: E2S147 belongs to optional-construction, E2S148 through E2S153 to const-generics, E2S154 through E2S157 to the Stage 2 parser, Text and List[Int] slices, and E2S158 to the call-arguments surface, and none is touched. The RFC narrows no production in spec/grammar.ebnf, so no currently-grammatical program becomes ungrammatical.
compatibility.corpus_query: git grep -hE '^let ' -- '*.kofun' | wc -l; git grep -lE '^let ' -- '*.kofun' | wc -l; git grep -hE '^let ' -- '*.kofun' | grep -vcE '^let [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* = -?[0-9]+$'

Of 75 top-level `let` declarations across 23 tracked `.kofun` sources, 73 are exactly `let NAME = <integer literal>` and are admitted by v1. The 2 exceptions are `let mut LIMIT = 1` and `let LIMIT = 1 + 2`, which are the refusal fixtures this slice adds, so the count of tracked sources outside the new fixtures requiring migration is 0. Restricted to the standard library the same query returns 61 declarations across 15 sources, all of them admitted.

rfcs.title: Derive v1 is a closed compiler-owned set, specified as the expansion a library derive would produce

compatibility.statement: `@derive` is refused today by tests/security/generated-meta-access.sh as a fail-closed producer boundary, so no program that compiles uses the surface and none can change meaning. New surface is the `@derive(...)` attribute on a `type` declaration, one closed-set member `eq` over concrete nominal records with `Int` or `Bool` fields, the `kofun expand` command, and the five codes E380 through E384. Those sit in a free band: E370 through E372 belong to RFC-0005 and E373 through E379 are unallocated, so nothing is touched. Generated declarations are ordinary declarations, so DD-032 coherence and the orphan rule apply to them unchanged rather than being widened.
